config.title: Advanced Patterns — Senior-Level Toolkit

intro.title: Advanced Patterns — Senior-Level Toolkit
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a small TypeScript application that demonstrates key advanced patterns used by senior developers, such as the Factory Pattern. You will learn how these patterns help create more flexible, maintainable, and scalable code. The core concepts involve using TypeScript's strong typing, interfaces, and classes to structure your program. By the end, you'll understand how to apply these patterns in your own projects to solve common design lessons effectively.
intro.usecase: This advanced TypeScript pattern toolkit is essential for building scalable enterprise applications like financial dashboards or e-commerce platforms. You'll use these patterns to create complex, type-safe data processing pipelines that handle real-time stock updates or shopping cart calculations. In UI components like interactive data tables with sorting and filtering, these patterns ensure maintainable code as features evolve. They're also crucial for building plugin architectures in developer tools or CMS systems where extensibility must remain type-safe.

objectives: Implement a generic utility type to enforce type constraints in a function.
Apply conditional types to create flexible type definitions based on input.
Construct a mapped type to transform the properties of an existing interface.
Configure a discriminated union to handle different shapes of data in a type-safe manner.
Manipulate type inference using the `infer` keyword within conditional types.
Integrate template literal types to generate dynamic string literal unions.
Initialize a type guard function to narrow types at runtime.

steps.instruction: Inside the AdvancedPatternsComponent, initialize a state object using Record<string, number> to store key-value pairs with specific types. Name this state variable 'counts'.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Create a type-safe handler function

steps.expectedOutcome: The component now contains a type-safe handler function that can be used to update state values.
successCriteria: A function named updateValue is defined with two typed parameters (key: string, value: string) and returns void.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but check that both parameters have explicit type annotations and the return type is void.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateValue function is not properly defined with typed parameters. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.instruction: Inside your component, create a generic utility function named transformData that accepts a parameter of a generic type T and returns a value of type T.
steps.hint: Define a function with a type parameter <T> before the parameter list. The function should take a parameter of type T and return the same type.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a generic function transformData that demonstrates type-safe data transformation using TypeScript generics.
successCriteria: The transformData function is defined with a generic type parameter <T>, accepts a parameter of type T, and returns a value of type T.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure transformData uses a generic type parameter <T> and both the parameter and return type are typed as T.
steps.feedbackWrong: The transformData function isn't properly defined. Remember to use a generic type parameter <T> and ensure the function signature accepts and returns the same type.
